answer: Carrier-checked phone binding: before an identity can earn, the network texts a one-time code to a mobile number and queries the carrier line-type record, rejecting VoIP ranges. A salted hash of each verified number may back only one active identity, so a farm needs a separate real SIM contract per account and pays its monthly fee. Splitting one operator into a nebula of accounts just multiplies that bill. Limits: one phone per person is a fable, since SIM farms resell numbers, and a painter selling pigment in a country without cheap lines gets excluded.
